> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3ca6108ae51364707b454aa4571cd42faec3a087` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `76111f57f5c1d757651909d4913bf100b70792db` — the merge of head `a69bdb8002e153d688d9ae96fe6d42eeecb16e26` into base `3ca6108ae51364707b454aa4571cd42faec3a087`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 76111f57f5c1d757651909d4913bf100b70792db && git checkout 76111f57f5c1d757651909d4913bf100b70792db
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3ca6108ae51364707b454aa4571cd42faec3a087 a69bdb8002e153d688d9ae96fe6d42eeecb16e26 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3ca6108ae51364707b454aa4571cd42faec3a087 && git merge --no-ff a69bdb8002e153d688d9ae96fe6d42eeecb16e26

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3ca6108ae51364707b454aa4571cd42faec3a087
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3ca6108ae51364707b454aa4571cd42faec3a087` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-e8-readers.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder.dogfood.test.ts, packages/rest/src/import-mapping.ts, packages/rest/src/import-integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.test.ts + (read, not reviewed) packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-mapping.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts (on main 7e8b31ce), docs/adr/0150 (D2, D3, D5, "A clash sealed before phase 1"); prose judged under ②: .changeset/32071-mapping-name-by-package.md, content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx, content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx

Inputs read: card #32071 body and all seven comments (claim 6760547602, ruling amendment 6760823385, os-dev-report 6762456462, carrier note 6763044616, takeover 6764439957, correction 6764689591, os-dev-report 6765942838); PR #32117 body, file list (10 files, +332/-10), net diff against merge-base 45f0f81f; the epic seat's records 6762480319 and 6765703642 (read as input on its red lines, not adopted). Check-runs on this head when read: every completed run is success or skipped, none failed (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, TypeScript Type Check, Lint and Repo Gates and all its Lint sub-jobs, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Build Docs, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, both PR-body guards runs: success). One `Check Changeset` run was still in_progress (the re-run after the body edit); the other `Check Changeset` run on the head is success.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Bare `GET /meta/mapping/NAME`, two package holders: 200 first-registered to 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming both. RIGHT. ADR-0150 D3 (a caller with no package: the environment item, else the unique package holder, else the refusal with candidates, 409 at a door) and D5 ("A bare address ... answers 409 with the candidate qualified addresses otherwise ... no new code is minted"). The one-line read-set entry routes `mapping` through the same `registry.resolveItem(type, name, null)` branch of `readMetaItem` the E8 types use; no new mechanism.
2. Qualified non-holder read (`?package=X`, `/meta/mapping/NS/NAME`, `/meta/mapping/_env/NAME`): 200 with the holder's item to 409 naming the holder. RIGHT, and not optional: D5's metadata row reads "`?package=X` kept as the exact qualifier: X's item with its bound overlay, or a refusal that names the holders, never X's closure". `admitExactQualifier` and `admitEnvironmentQualifier` are both gated on `registry.readsByPackage(type)`, so this follows from the read-set entry and cannot be carved out without a second set. It was not on the ruling's FROM/TO list; it is declared as item 4 in the changeset and PR body. Accepted as declared (answers the dev's open question 2 with A).
3. Import door `mappingName`, two holders: 200 or 400 `MAPPING_TARGET_MISMATCH` to 409 naming both, nothing written. RIGHT against ruling Q1-A. The catch returns `err.status`, `err.code`, `err.message`; no literal. The refusal is thrown before any layer is read and `resolveNamedMapping` runs before the runner, so no row can be written.
4. Connector pull, two holders: pulling through the first holder to a thrown `ConnectorPullError` with the read's own code and status and reason `mapping_name_refused`. RIGHT against ruling Q2-A. `return refuse(...)` sits in the catch body, so the throw leaves the try/catch and is not swallowed; it precedes connector resolution, the action call and `runImport`. The name is sound: it sits beside `mapping_not_found` and follows the existing `mapping_target_refused` / `mapping_apply_refused` pattern (answers open question 1 with A; the seat confirms at ACCEPT).
5. Every other error still answers not-found (404 `MAPPING_NOT_FOUND` / `mapping_not_found`). RIGHT against the ruling ("Every other error keeps today's answer"). With no caller package the only reason the resolver can return is `ambiguous-in-environment`, so no other refusal reason is being collapsed. A degraded-store read still answering 404 is pre-existing and outside this card.
6. No other by-name reader of `mapping` exists in the tree (grep of `type: 'mapping'` and facade reads: only these two), and the save door reads the prior item for `object` only, so no write door of `mapping` changes answer.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on objectql, rest and service-automation with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct under AGENTS.md step 3 (a non-protocol breaking change ships patch and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition). Nothing an author can write changes. Exactly one marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with a true reason. `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` are untouched and rightly absent.
- FROM to TO completeness: the four changed answers I could derive from the tree are the four the changeset lists, each with its one-line fix. I found no undeclared served-to-refused or 404-to-409 answer. The 404-to-409 framing in the code comment is not a wire FROM (no two-holder request answered 404 before; the first holder was served), and the changeset states the true FROM.
- Docs: both pages match the diff. `import-mappings.mdx` (resolution paragraph, the 409 row "and the environment holds none") and `jobs.mdx` (refused before any call or write, run `failed`) agree with D3 and with `pullConnectorSource` rethrowing. `Skills-docs: updated here` is true; `git grep` of `mappingName`, `pull.mapping`, `connectorSource` under `skills/` at this head is empty.
- `Part of #32071` is right: no closing keyword in title or body, the card is open, and nothing in the diff, changeset or docs claims the pull-by-job-package half (both docs say the pull "cannot yet read its own package's mapping"). `callerPackageId` is not read anywhere in this diff.
- should-fix S1 — `Narrowing: no` beside `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is unexplained and, read against ADR-0150, wrong. The ADR's "A clash sealed before phase 1" paragraph says a no-package caller refused on a pre-existing two-holder name is declared in the child's `Narrowing:` line with its measured count, and the carrier note 6763044616 item 2 uses the line in that sense. This PR is exactly that narrowing (plus the D5 exact qualifier). The line was copied from ruling amendment 6760823385, where the likely intent was "none of D3 (a)/(c): no package caller is wired". Not graded must-fix because the narrowing is fully declared in the arm, the BREAKING list and the changeset, and the line does not ship; but the PR body is the record. Fix by body edit, no new head: state the sealed-clash and exact-qualifier narrowings with first-party count 0, and say (a)/(c) are none because no reader here has a package caller.
- nit N1 — the changeset names the new reason but has no TypeScript note that the exported union `ConnectorPullRefusalReason` gains a member (the package's CHANGELOG precedent for `input_schema_mismatch` carried one; an exhaustive switch in a consumer stops compiling).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (reason name) and 2 (FROM to TO 4): answered in ① items 4 and 2. The epic seat agreed on 2 and left the line to the seat.
- os-dev-report 6762456462 out-of-scope items: the read-set conflict with #32092 is resolved at this head (both `api` and `mapping` kept, pin expects both); the docs follow-up is discharged in this head.
- Carrier note 6763044616: items 1 and 2 belong to the pull-half PR and nothing here pre-empts them. should-fix S2 — item 3 is undisposed. It asks that the `callerPackageId` TSDoc sentence ("exactly as today — the bare name, read as a caller with no package") and its doc pin be updated "once this card makes the caller-less read D3's", and this PR is the one that does. The takeover lists the note as read; neither report nor the PR body says where item 3 goes. `packages/spec` is outside this PR's file surface and would change its face, so it should not be fixed here; the seat records on the card that item 3 is owed by the pull-half PR (or a spec-lane card). My reading is that the sentence stays literally true after landing, which is why this is not a must-fix.
- should-fix S3 — stale on landing. #32114 merged to main after this head's merge-base (45f0f81f; main is now 7e8b31ce, merge is clean). On the landed tree `ConnectorSourcePullRequest` carries `callerPackageId`, so the parentheses "(the pull request carries none)" in `connector-pull.ts` and "(its request carries none)" in `connector-pull.test.ts` are false; the true statement is that the pull does not read it yet. The seat already expects one more main merge for #32097; fix the wording then.
- Deviations (body edit by the card thread on the seat's order, attribution block, amended unpublished merge commit): process, no contract effect.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on main: it makes the spec's own refusal real. ADR-0150 D3 and D5 already publish "never the first match, 409 naming candidates" for a no-package read; the cold boot only warns on this shape; the first-party count is 0. It takes no declared capability away at a consumer: every one-holder answer is untouched, including the case ruling Q1 exists to protect.

- `package-scoped-read.ts`: holds. One entry; header and TSDoc match the tree.
- `import-mapping.ts`: holds. Tried: two holders (refused, own code and status); one holder; one holder into another package's object (served: the door names no caller, so no `outside-closure`); refusal swallowed (no: early return in the catch).
- `connector-pull.ts`: holds. Production passes the real `protocol` service straight into the pull (`plugin.ts`), so the class reaches the catch unwrapped.
- should-fix S4 (both readers) — the catch is `instanceof PackageScopedNameRefusedError` only. The `/meta` door's own catcher (`isPackageScopedRefusal`, runtime `domains/meta.ts`) also matches by shape (`code === 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'` and `refusal.status === 'refused'`), and plugin-approvals reads the refusal by shape. If the throwing and catching packages ever hold different copies of `@objectstack/core` (dual CJS/ESM load, two installed versions), these two readers fall through to `404 MAPPING_NOT_FOUND` / `mapping_not_found`, the exact answer the ruling forbids. It still fails closed (never the first holder), hence should-fix. Add the shape fallback.
- Tests, ADR-0112: `code` and `status` are asserted at each door. objectql: both protocol faces and the facade, two holders, per-package and exact reads, one-holder CONTROL equal to `getItem`, environment item, zero holders. rest: `[409, RESOURCE_CONFLICT]`, both ids in the message, no row; one-holder CONTROL writes. service-automation: over a real `SchemaRegistry` and real protocol; reason, code, 409, both ids, no handler call, no write; one-holder CONTROL. Dogfood: bare 409 naming both; qualified and `?package=` reach each holder; import 409 into either holder's object; non-holder qualified 409 naming zeta; CONTROL with zeta into `alpha_item` 200 and into `beta_item` still 400 `MAPPING_TARGET_MISMATCH`.
- nit N2 — the `_env` form of FROM to TO 4 is declared but not pinned for `mapping` (the dogfood pins the namespace and `?package=` forms). The mechanism is type-generic.
- nit N3 — no pin for "the environment holds the name and two packages hold it too: the environment's is served", the case the new docs row's "and the environment holds none" rests on; `mapping` is runtime-creatable, so this is the type where it is most likely. The resolver's order is pinned generically in core.
- nit N4 — the service-automation pin compares `err.code` to the read's own `code`, not to the literal; the literal is pinned in objectql, rest and dogfood.
- Not verified, stated plainly: the byte-identity of one-holder answers (the base-versus-head probe) and the ablation results are the dev's reported runs; I ran nothing. What I checked is that the code path for one holder is the same resolver answer the layers served before and that the CONTROL tests assert it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `24baf39c78690980a128a0ba4a841f2a4771917a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-e8-readers.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder.dogfood.test.ts, packages/rest/src/import-mapping.ts, packages/rest/src/import-integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.test.ts + (read, not reviewed) packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts; prose judged under ②: .changeset/32071-mapping-name-by-package.md

Delta record. The PASS on `eae53a29` (card comment 6766076903) stands for everything this delta does not touch. The delta is two commits: the merge 02300a74 of `origin/main` at e0a78783, and the fix commit 24baf39c (five files: the changeset, the two readers and their two tests).

Inputs read: the fix commit's diff; the merge result's net diff against its merge-base compared with the old head's net diff; the PR body as it is now; card #32071 comments after 6765942838 (only the review claim and my earlier record; no new os-dev-report); the epic seat's delta read 6767358248 (input only). Check-runs on this head: 53 runs, every one completed as success or skipped; none failed, none in progress.

### ① Derived judgments

1. S4 (shape-fallback catch): CLOSED in both readers. `packageScopedRefusalOf` in `import-mapping.ts` and `connector-pull.ts` matches by class, else by `code === 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'` and `refusal.status === 'refused'`.
2. The predicate matches runtime `domains/meta.ts` `isPackageScopedRefusal` exactly: the same two conditions, joined the same way, nothing added and nothing dropped. It is not broader. A `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with no `refusal`, or with a `refusal` of another status, returns `undefined` and keeps the 404 / `mapping_not_found` answer.
3. What the helper adds beyond the predicate is only how the answer is read off a shape-matched error: `status`, else `httpStatus`, else 409; `message`, else `refusal.message`. The 409 default is the class's only status, so it mints nothing.
4. Merge: every read-set entry kept. `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES` on main at the merge-base is E8's nine plus `api`; at this head it is those ten plus `mapping`. No other landing had added an entry (#32097 has not landed; main at 171cf6d9 still ends at `api`). `LATER_TYPES` is `['api', 'mapping']` and the pin expects E8 plus both.
5. No conflict-resolution regression: the merge result's net diff against its merge-base is identical to the old head's net diff, apart from a two-line offset in `jobs.mdx` from main's own edit above the hunk.
6. New FROM to TO: none. A shape-matched refusal moving from 404 to 409 is the declared two-holder refusal reaching the door through another copy of the class, not a new answer.
